themeCards.title: Waller opened a hold path, and the front end followed
themeCards.fact: Waller: if inflation data due over the next two weeks keep cooling, he is inclined to hold; if August inflation is hot, a hike at the 15–16 September FOMC may be appropriate. Kitco: the S&P 500 closed at 7,747.71, up 1.1%, and FedWatch’s September hike odds fell to 50.4% from 63.2% Wednesday. US Treasury: the official 3 September curve printed 4.34% on the 2-year and 4.77% on the 10-year. ISM: August services PMI 55.4 after 54.1, with prices paid at 72.6, the highest since August 2022.
themeCards.mechanism: A named hold-if-CPI reaction function is what cut hike odds and pulled the 2-year to 4.34%, which is why the S&P 500 could post a one-month bounce even with services still expanding. CICC (4 September): the September hike is two-sided on the data, and a hike can still be the credibility path unless payrolls and CPI cooperate. August employment at 20:30 Beijing on 4 September, then CPI on 11 September, then the FOMC at 02:00 Beijing on 17 September, are the settle.

themeCards.title: The yen kept rising, and Tokyo’s FX chief is still not satisfied
themeCards.fact: 财经早茶 国际要闻: the yen extended its rebound, traders raised BOJ hike bets, and Japan’s top FX official said he is neither reassured nor satisfied. Cointelegraph: USD/JPY printed 155.4 after 158.5 on Wednesday. Kyodo: Mimura stays on high alert, with the dollar in the lower 156 yen range and the BOJ meeting on 17–18 September. 财经新闻: the Nikkei 225 closed at 64,214.48, down 0.17%.
themeCards.mechanism: A second day of yen strength with Mimura still unsatisfied keeps intervention risk and a September BOJ hike in the same trade, which is why USD/JPY can run even when the Nikkei only slips 0.17%. Until the Ministry of Finance confirms it sold dollars, this remains a threat traders price rather than a dated print. The BOJ decision on 17–18 September is the settle.

themeCards.title: Oil held a war premium after Iran fired at Kuwait
themeCards.fact: CNBC: WTI settled at $91.30, up 29 cents, and Brent at $95.52, down 11 cents, after Iran fired missiles toward Kuwait. 财经早茶 能源: crude futures rose slightly as Iran said it struck US bases in Kuwait and the UAE. 律动: Oman rejected Iran’s proposal to charge commercial ships service fees in Hormuz.
themeCards.mechanism: A 29-cent WTI uptick after another Gulf strike is the market holding the premium, not adding to it, so oil is still a geopolitics book rather than a Waller duration book. Oman refusing Hormuz fees leaves the strait without a fee regime and without a dated flow print that would let $91 go. The next dated Hormuz or OPEC+ flow print, and CPI on 11 September through the energy line, are what settle whether this premium sticks.

themeCards.title: Gold and bitcoin both caught the softer-dollar bounce
themeCards.fact: Kitco: late-afternoon spot gold was near $4,471.10, up 1.92%, after a $4,511.70 high. Cointelegraph: bitcoin reached $81,000 in US hours, up about 5%. 律动: Glassnode still sees resistance at 83,000 to 86,000, with US spot ETF 7-day average inflows peaking at $290 million against about $3 billion of secondary volume.
themeCards.mechanism: Both assets trade the same Waller duration and dollar beta, so gold and bitcoin rose together when hike odds fell, but bitcoin still sits under a 83,000–86,000 supply zone that ETF inflows have not cleared. CICC (21 August): stay overweight gold because Treasury long-bond buybacks weaken dollar and Treasury credibility, a bid bitcoin does not get; Glassnode (2 September): spot is boxed between short-term-holder supply below and long-term-holder supply above. Payrolls tonight, through the dollar, are the next print.

themeCards.title: Beijing advertised an SME fund while the PBOC drained again
themeCards.fact: 第一财经: ten ministries will set up the national SME development fund phase two. 新华财经: 3 September reverse-repo operations were zero against 1030亿元 maturing, a net drain of 1030亿元 (CNY103.0bn). 证券日报: Shanghai closed at 3942.09, up 0.02%. 财经早茶 今日图表: Longsys A-shares ran far ahead of a flat STAR 50 into the Hong Kong listing.
themeCards.mechanism: A second straight zero-ops day is a tighter onshore mix than the SME-fund headline, which is why Shanghai could only add 0.02% while the chart tells a one-name story rather than an index one. Morgan Stanley (4 September): it cut China and Hong Kong index targets on worsening macro data and tightening liquidity, while CICC (2 September): swap-implied rate-cut expectations already sit at a historically strong level, so the drain lands between a street that has lowered its targets and a rates market still paying for a cut. The next PBOC take-up and tonight’s US payrolls, through risk appetite, are the dated prints.
